adjudications.why: Solver chose (C). (C) as printed pairs the animals wrongly (horses with bulldogs, donkeys with spaniels), so it misstates the passage. The passage's test for a species is whether DNA can pass between two kinds of animal: mutations in donkey DNA can never cross to horses, while a bulldog and a spaniel share one DNA pool. Key (B) stands.
adjudications.solution:
The passage defines a species by whether two kinds of animal **share one DNA pool**. Horses and donkeys can be made to mate, but their offspring (mules) are sterile, so a mutation in donkey DNA can never reach horses. That is why they are two species. A bulldog and a spaniel look very different, yet they belong to one species because they share the same DNA pool.

So the classification turns on the shared DNA pool, which is option (B).

Option (C) sounds close, but it pairs the animals wrongly: the passage sets horses and donkeys against bulldogs and spaniels, not horses and bulldogs against donkeys and spaniels. Options (A) and (D) talk about behaviour and the environment, which the passage does not use.

So the answer is option (B).

adjudications.why: Solver chose (D) 2009, reading 'first time' as the passage's phrase about the four-year run. The question asks when freedom first declined; the passage says 2009 was the FOURTH consecutive year of decline, so the decline began in 2006. Key (C) is the intended reading of a loosely worded stem.
adjudications.solution:
The last paragraph says that 2009 was the **fourth year in a row** in which freedom declined around the world.

Count back four years: the declines were in 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009. So the decline began in **2006**, option (C).

Option (D), 2009, is the year Freedom House reported the four-year run, not the year the decline started. Option (A), 1973, is when Freedom House began its measurements, and nothing in the passage points to 1990.

So the answer is option (C).
